title: Characteristic-zero enveloping algebra realization by distributions
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a smooth affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $C=k[G]$, $\varepsilon:C\to k$ for evaluation at the identity, $I=\ker\varepsilon$, and $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_k C$ for the coordinate map of multiplication. Define
$$\operatorname{Dist}(G)=\bigcup_{n\geq0}\operatorname{Hom}_k(C/I^{n+1},k),\qquad (ab)(f)=(a\otimes b)(\Delta f),$$
with identity $\varepsilon$. Identify $\mathfrak l=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ with the linear maps $v:C\to k$ satisfying $v(fg)=\varepsilon(f)v(g)+v(f)\varepsilon(g)$, with the tangent Lie bracket; equivalently it is the commutator bracket of the left-invariant derivations $D_v=(\operatorname{id}\otimes v)\Delta$. A Lie algebra has the meaning of [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Let $U_k(\mathfrak l)=T_k(\mathfrak l)/(xy-yx-[x,y]:x,y\in\mathfrak l)$. There is a unital $k$-algebra isomorphism
$$\Theta_G:U_k(\mathfrak l)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Dist}(G)$$
whose value on a generator $v$ is the same functional $v:C\to k$. It is natural for homomorphisms of smooth affine finite-type $k$-groups: for $f:G\to G'$ one has
$$f_*\Theta_G=\Theta_{G'}U_k(df),\qquad (f_*a)(h)=a(f^*h).$$
Here $U_k(df)$ is the algebra homomorphism induced by $df$ on the tensor-algebra quotients. No connectedness or semisimplicity assumption on $G$ is required.

source.place: Section 10l, printed p.208: the natural inclusion of the tangent Lie algebra into distributions extends to the characteristic-zero enveloping-algebra isomorphism. Naturality follows from its values on generators and the tensor-quotient universal property.

proof.text: The coordinate maps satisfy the commutative Hopf algebra axioms: the group diagrams become coassociativity, counit and antipode identities on functions. Apply [lem-sfb-bialgebra-distribution-tangent-calculus] to identify the displayed union with the filtered algebra $F=\bigcup F_n$ and to identify its tangent-functionals bracket with convolution commutator. Thus $v\mapsto v$ is a Lie map $\mathfrak l\to F$ for the bracket specified in the statement.

source.place: Section 10l, printed p.208, applying Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; Theorem 10.36, printed pp.200--204

proof.text: Send a tensor word $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_r$ to $v_1*\cdots*v_r$, and the empty word to $\varepsilon$, extending linearly on each tensor degree and the direct sum. Multilinearity gives a map on tensor products; concatenation becomes multiplication. Each defining relation maps to $v*w-w*v-[v,w]=0$ by Step 1. The map therefore descends to a unital algebra map $\Theta:U_k(\mathfrak l)\to F$, with the required generator values. Any map with these values agrees on every tensor word, so is unique.

source.place: Section 10l, printed p.208, applying Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; Theorem 10.36, printed pp.200--204

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-augmentation-monomial-pairing] to $C$. Choose lifts $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ of its cotangent basis. The corresponding $v_i$ form a basis of $\mathfrak l=(I/I^2)^*$ by [lem-sfb-bialgebra-distribution-tangent-calculus]. Characteristic zero gives $n!\ne0$ for every $n$, so the degree-$n$ coordinate monomials form a basis of $I^n/I^{n+1}$. By [lem-sfb-field-filtered-pbw], the ordered words $E^a=j(v_1)^{a_1}\cdots j(v_d)^{a_d}$ with $|a|\le n$ form a basis of $U_{\le n}$, and those of degree exactly $n$ give its successive quotient basis.

source.place: Section 10l, printed p.208, applying Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; Theorem 10.36, printed pp.200--204

proof.text: For $n\ge1$, restriction to $I^n$ gives a surjection $F_n\to(I^n/I^{n+1})^*$ with kernel $F_{n-1}$: extend a functional from the subspace $I^n/I^{n+1}\subset C/I^{n+1}$ by a vector-space basis. Since $\mathfrak l\subseteq F_1$ and $F_r*F_s\subseteq F_{r+s}$ by [lem-sfb-bialgebra-distribution-tangent-calculus], $\Theta(U_{\le n})\subseteq F_n$, so $\Theta$ is filtered. The factorial pairing in [lem-sfb-hopf-augmentation-monomial-pairing] says its degree-$n$ matrix in the Step-3 bases is diagonal with nonzero entries $\prod a_i!$. Hence each successive quotient map is bijective. At $n=0$, $C/I=k$ and $\Theta(c)=c\varepsilon$, so the filtration-zero map is bijective.

source.place: Section 10l, printed p.208, applying Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; Theorem 10.36, printed pp.200--204

proof.text: Induct on $n$ to prove $\Theta:U_{\le n}\to F_n$ bijective. The base is Step 4. Given $b\in F_n$, lift its quotient class by the bijective degree-$n$ map; subtract that lift's image and use surjectivity at $n-1$. If an element has zero image, its degree-$n$ class is zero by injectivity on that quotient, so it belongs to $U_{\le n-1}$ and vanishes by induction. Every tensor quotient element and every distribution belongs to a finite filtration step. Thus $\Theta$ is bijective on the unions and is the claimed algebra isomorphism. The same argument covers $d=0$, where the positive quotient bases are empty.

source.place: Section 10l, printed p.208, applying Lemma 11.27, printed p.218; Theorem 10.36, printed pp.200--204

proof.text: For a group homomorphism $f:G\to G'$, its coordinate map $q=f^*$ satisfies $\varepsilon q=\varepsilon'$ and $\Delta q=(q\otimes q)\Delta'$. Thus $q(I')\subset I$, so precomposition sends $F_n(G)$ into $F_n(G')$. For $h\in k[G']$, $(f_*(a*b))(h)=(a\otimes b)((q\otimes q)\Delta'h)=((f_*a)*(f_*b))(h)$, and $f_*\varepsilon=\varepsilon'$. On tangent functionals this map is $df(v)=v q$, so the commutator formula of Step 1 shows it preserves brackets. The tensor-word construction of Step 2 therefore defines $U_k(df)$. Both sides of the claimed naturality equation send each generator $v$ to $vq$; they agree on every word and hence everywhere. Neither this calculation nor Steps 1--5 uses connectedness or semisimplicity.

lean.statement: theorem characteristicZero_distribution_enveloping (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) [IsAffine G.X.left] [Smooth G.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom] : ∃ ΘG : UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra k (tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G)) ≃ₐ[k] distributionAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G), (∀ (v : tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G)) (c : coordinateAlgebra G), (ΘG (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι k v)).val c = v.val c) ∧ ∀ (H : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) [IsAffine H.X.left] [Smooth H.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType H.X.hom] [QuasiCompact H.X.hom], ∃ ΘH : UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra k (tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra H)) ≃ₐ[k] distributionAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra H), (∀ (v : tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra H)) (c : coordinateAlgebra H), (ΘH (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι k v)).val c = v.val c) ∧ ∀ f : G ⟶ H, ∃ (push : distributionAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G) →ₐ[k] distributionAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra H)) (df : tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G) →ₗ⁅k⁆ tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra H)) (Udf : UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra k (tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G)) →ₐ[k] UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra k (tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra H))), (∀ (a : distributionAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G)) (c : coordinateAlgebra H), (push a).val c = a.val (coordinateMap f c)) ∧ (∀ (v : tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G)) (c : coordinateAlgebra H), (df v).val c = v.val (coordinateMap f c)) ∧ (∀ v : tangentLieAlgebra k (coordinateAlgebra G), Udf (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι k v) = UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι k (df v)) ∧ push.comp ΘG.toAlgHom = ΘH.toAlgHom.comp Udf
